overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by untimely approving August 2022 minutes (intentionally, though no civil penalty) and by omitting candidate names from a notice, but not by the liquor-license notice wording.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to timely approve the minutes of its August 8 and August 22, 2022 meetings; the AG also found the violation intentional.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board did not approve the August 8 and August 22 meeting minutes until October 3, 56 days after its August 8 meeting, and 42 days after its August 22 meeting, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve these minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 3, 2022 notice failed to list candidates to be approved or appointed (a police dispatcher and a Board of Health member).
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the October 3, 2022 notice was insufficiently specific because it omitted the date of the Rehoboth People Have Heart one-day liquor license event.
allegations.key_passage: Although listing additional detail may have been helpful to the public, we are satisfied that the topic as listed was sufficient to reasonably advise the public of the issue to be discussed at the meeting.

remedy: Create and approve all outstanding meeting minutes within ninety (90) days of the Board's receipt of this letter, and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to create and approve all outstanding meeting minutes within ninety (90) days of the Board's receipt of this letter, and to certify to our office that it has done so. We also order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
